sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Roman Chair Ab Crunch is an abdominal exercise performed on a Roman chair (captain's chair) station where you support yourself on forearm pads and lift your knees toward your chest.

This exercise primarily targets the rectus abdominis and hip flexors, with the hanging position increasing the range of motion and difficulty compared to floor-based crunches.

It is an effective bodyweight movement for building core strength and definition without the need for additional equipment.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Effectively isolates the abdominal muscles
- Greater range of motion than traditional floor crunches
- No additional equipment needed beyond the Roman chair
- Reduces strain on the neck and lower back compared to sit-ups
- Builds functional core strength for everyday activities
- Can be progressed by adding ankle weights or slowing the tempo
- Suitable for intermediate to advanced fitness levels

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Rectus Abdominis, Hip Flexors

Secondary: Obliques, Transverse Abdominis, Forearms (stabilization)

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Step onto the Roman chair and position your forearms on the armrests.
2. Press your back firmly against the backrest pad.
3. Grip the handles for stability.
4. Allow your legs to hang straight down, feet off the ground.
5. Engage your core and maintain a neutral spine before beginning.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Engage your core muscles and brace your abs.
2. Exhale as you lift your knees towards your chest in a controlled motion.
3. Focus on curling your pelvis upward to maximize abdominal contraction.
4. Pause briefly at the top of the movement, squeezing your abs.
5. Inhale as you slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.
6. Avoid swinging or using momentum to lift your legs.
7. Repeat the movement for the desired number of reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Swinging the legs using momentum instead of controlled movement
- Not lifting the knees high enough to fully engage the abs
- Arching the lower back away from the pad
- Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
- Using the hip flexors exclusively instead of engaging the abs
- Dropping the legs too quickly on the lowering phase
- Holding breath throughout the movement
- Gripping the handles too tightly, creating unnecessary tension

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Roman Chair (Captain's Chair) Station
- Optional: Ankle Weights (for added resistance)
- Optional: Medicine Ball (held between knees for progression)

sections.heading: Machine Setup
sections.content:
1. Adjust the armrest height if the machine allows it.
2. Ensure the backrest pad is secure and in good condition.
3. Check that the handles are clean and provide a solid grip.
4. Position yourself so your forearms rest comfortably on the pads.
5. Your back should be flat against the backrest when in the starting position.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Forearms: Resting flat on the armrest pads.
2. Hands: Gripping the handles firmly but not excessively.
3. Back: Pressed flat against the backrest pad.
4. Shoulders: Down and relaxed, away from ears.
5. Legs: Hanging straight down, feet together.
6. Core: Engaged and braced before initiating the movement.
7. Head: Neutral position, looking straight ahead.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Hanging Leg Raise: Performed from a pull-up bar for greater difficulty
- Bodyweight Crunch: Floor-based alternative for beginners
- Cable Crunch: Adjustable resistance using a cable machine
- Decline Sit-Up: Bench-based crunch with gravity assistance
- Ab Wheel Rollout: Advanced core exercise for full abdominal engagement
- Lying Leg Raise: Floor-based lower ab focus

sections.heading: Roman Chair Variations
sections.content:
Roman Chair Knee Raise: Standard knee-to-chest movement
Roman Chair Straight Leg Raise: Legs kept straight for increased difficulty
Roman Chair Oblique Raise: Knees raised to one side for oblique activation
Roman Chair Bicycle: Alternating knee drives mimicking cycling motion
Weighted Roman Chair Crunch: Ankle weights or medicine ball for progression
Slow Tempo Roman Chair Crunch: Extended lowering phase for time under tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Issues: Ensure armrests are adjusted to reduce shoulder strain
Lower Back Pain: Keep back firmly pressed against the pad at all times
Hip Flexor Tightness: Focus on pelvic tilt rather than knee height
Grip Fatigue: Use wrist wraps or padded handles
No Roman Chair Available: Substitute with hanging knee raises or floor crunches
Learning Stage: Start with small knee raises and gradually increase range of motion
